AN OPEN LETTER TO VICE PRESIDENT JD VANCE

Fix the System, Not the People: Securing American Tech Supremacy and Stopping the Outsourcing Loophole

Dear Vice President Vance,

For decades, America has enjoyed the greatest free lunch in economic history: the world’s sharpest, most highly educated minds bringing their talent, patents, and relentless ambition directly to our shores. Yet today, Washington is snatching defeat from the jaws of victory. By subjecting elite global engineers to broken lotteries and multi-decade backlogs, the current immigration system actively deters the very talent required to keep America first in AI, quantum computing, and advanced engineering.
It is time for a clear-eyed policy shift that cuts through political soundbites: Fix the broken system, do not target the people who are building American wealth.

Stop Mislabeling the People: Skilled Talent Is Not "Indentured Labor"
Using tropes like "indentured labor" to describe world-class Indian engineers and researchers is not only historically inaccurate—it misdiagnoses the entire problem. Indenture was a system of colonial coercion; today’s high-skilled immigrants are top-tier professionals earning six-figure salaries, fueling enterprise innovation, and contributing billions in taxes to the American economy.
When politicians attack the people instead of the rules, they miss the core issue: The problem is not high-skilled immigration; the problem is system gaming by low-wage body shops.

Frontier Innovation vs. The Outsourcing Body Shops

American technology powerhouses do not recruit Indian H-1B engineers to cheapen labor—they do so because the depth of specialized mathematical and engineering capacity simply does not exist in required numbers domestically.
Indian technical professionals bring an extraordinary standard of work ethic: exceptional mathematical grounding, adaptability, and an unyielding commitment to execution. In high-stakes engineering cycles—whether training multi-billion parameter AI models, scaling hyperscale cloud infrastructure, or troubleshooting critical hardware—they bring focus, discipline, and grit. They aren't taking five coffee breaks and two-hour lunches; they are in the trenches shipping product.

The real threat to American workers comes from IT intermediary body shops—high-volume outsourcing firms that flood the randomized H-1B lottery to land entry-level maintenance contracts, undercut domestic wages, and generate no original intellectual property.
Frontier product leaders hire at top salary tiers (Wage Level 3 and Level 4) to drive advanced R&D and build U.S. intellectual property. Conversely, IT outsourcing intermediaries rely on entry-level wage bands (Level 1 and Level 2) and high-volume lottery manipulation for commoditized IT maintenance.

Shut down the body shops exploiting low-wage loopholes. Do not penalize the product innovators building the technology that underpins American GDP.
The ROI of Indian-Origin Talent: By the Numbers
The evidence that global intellect—and Indian brainpower in particular—drives American hegemony is undeniable:

Trillion-Dollar Leadership: Indian-origin CEOs lead tech titans including Microsoft, Alphabet (Google), Adobe, IBM, Micron, and Palo Alto Networks—companies that collectively command over $5 Trillion in market capitalization.
